title: Conselhos
goal: Aluno sai sabendo dar conselhos com should/shouldn't e falar de obrigações com have to/don't have to.
connects_to: M21 (Se isso, então aquilo) — depois de conselhos, aprende condicionais reais.
module_chunks: You should / She should / He should
I should + base / She should + base
I have to / You have to / She has to
I don't have to / She doesn't have to
Do I have to...? / Does she have to...?
You should see a doctor / You should study more
I have to work / She has to leave

units.title: Você deveria descansar
units.real_life_context: Você dá e recebe conselhos sobre saúde, estudo, vida.

grammar.explanation: "Should" = deveria. Aconselhamento positivo: "You should see a doctor".
"Shouldn't / Should not" = não deveria. Aconselhamento negativo.
"We should help" = nós deveríamos ajudar.
"He shouldn't / should not eat junk food" = ele não deveria.
"You should study" = você deveria estudar.
"She shouldn't / should not stay up late" = ela não deveria ficar acordada.
"I think you should try" = acho que você deveria tentar.
Modal "should" não leva -s na 3ª pessoa. "She should", não "She shoulds".

grammar.sentence: You should to see a doctor.
grammar.explanation: Modal + base, sem "to": "should see", não "should to see".

grammar.passage: I think you should rest more. You shouldn't work so late. We should all take breaks.
grammar.question: O que a pessoa não deveria fazer?
grammar.explanation: O texto diz "You shouldn't / should not work so late".

roleplay.scenario: Charlotte conta um problema — você dá conselho.
roleplay.opening_line: I'm tired and stressed. What should I do?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user gives advice with 'You should + base'
user advises against with 'You shouldn't + base'
user gives another advice with should/shouldn't

roleplay.closing_cue: Charlotte fecha com "Wise advice!" quando obj_3 baterem.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Charlotte**: "I'm tired and stressed. What should I do?"
2. **Student**: ~"You should rest."
3. **Charlotte**: "I have a lot of work though."
4. **Student**: ~"You shouldn't work so much."
5. **Charlotte**: "Anything else?"
6. **Student**: ~"You should take a vacation."
7. **Charlotte**: "Wise advice!"

guided_chat.intro_pt: Charlotte abre chat pedindo conselho. Pratica should/shouldn't.
guided_chat.opening_message: I want to learn English faster. Any advice?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses 'You should + base'
user uses 'You shouldn't + base'

objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks 'What should I + base?' or 'Any other tips?'

guided_chat.closing_cue: Charlotte encerra com "Great advice exchange!" quando obj_3 baterem.
guided_chat.suggested_script:

1. **Charlotte**: "I want to learn English faster. Any advice?"

units.title: Tenho que trabalhar
units.real_life_context: Você fala de obrigações no trabalho, escola, casa.

grammar.explanation: "Have to" pra obrigação. Com I/you/we/they: "have to + base".
"She has to" — 3ª pessoa usa "has to". Mesmo padrão do present simple.
"We have to" — plural usa "have to".
He → "has to". 3ª pessoa singular.
"I have to finish" — obrigação.
Lucas = he → "has to".
"They have to" — plural.
She → "has to", não "have to". 3ª pessoa singular.
Com I sempre "have", não "has".

grammar.passage: I have to work tomorrow. My sister has to study for an exam. We all have to wake up early.
grammar.question: O que a irmã tem que fazer?
grammar.explanation: O texto diz "My sister has to study for an exam".

listening_speaking.text: He has to go to the doctor.
They have to wake up early.

units.title: Não preciso fazer isso
units.grammar_focus: Don't have to / doesn't have to (absence of obligation)
units.real_life_context: Você esclarece que algo é OPCIONAL — não é obrigado a fazer.

grammar.sentence: I _____ have to work on Sundays.
grammar.explanation: Negativa: "don't / do not have to" = não precisa. Com I/you/we/they.
3ª pessoa: "doesn't / does not have to".
"We don't / do not have to" — plural.

grammar.sentence: He _____ have to wear a tie.
grammar.explanation: "He doesn't / does not have to" — 3ª pessoa.
"I don't / do not have to" — ausência de obrigação.

grammar.sentence: She _____ have to wake up early.
grammar.explanation: "She doesn't / does not have to" — 3ª pessoa.

grammar.sentence: You _____ have to come if you don't want.
grammar.explanation: "You don't / do not have to come" — opcional.
She → "doesn't / does not", não "don't / do not".
Com I sempre "don't / do not", não "doesn't / does not".

grammar.passage: I don't have to work tomorrow — it's my day off. She doesn't have to come if she's busy. We don't have to do anything special.
grammar.question: Por que o narrador não precisa trabalhar amanhã?
grammar.explanation: O texto diz "it's / it is my day off".

listening_speaking.text: I don't have to work on Sundays.
He doesn't have to wear a tie.

units.title: Devo ir? Tenho que ir?
units.real_life_context: Você pede conselho ou esclarece obrigações.

grammar.explanation: "Should I + base?" — pedido de conselho.
"Should she leave?" — pedido de conselho em 3ª pessoa. Should não muda.

grammar.sentence: _____ I have to bring my passport?
grammar.explanation: "Do I have to + base?" — pergunta sobre obrigação. Usa "do".
"Does she have to?" — 3ª pessoa pergunta com "does".
"Should I help you?" — oferta polida.

grammar.sentence: _____ he take a taxi or walk?
grammar.explanation: "Should he take a taxi?" — pedido de conselho sobre ele.

grammar.sentence: _____ I have to wear a tie?
grammar.explanation: "Do I have to?" — "Have to" usa do/does em perguntas.
Modal "should" forma pergunta por inversão direta — sem "do".
Have to pergunta com do/does, não "has". "Does she have to?".

grammar.passage: Q: Should I call her? A: Yes, you should. Q: Do I have to bring my passport? A: No, you don't have to.
grammar.question: A pessoa precisa trazer o passaporte?
grammar.explanation: The text says "No, you don't / do not have to".

listening_speaking.text: Do I have to bring my passport?

units.title: Dever, precisar, sugerir
units.grammar_focus: Integration should + have to + need to
units.real_life_context: Você combina os três modais pra falar de vida real — obrigações fortes, conselhos, necessidades.

grammar.sentence: You _____ rest more — it's a suggestion.
grammar.explanation: "Should" = sugestão/conselho leve. "Have to" e "need to" são mais fortes.
"Have to" = obrigação externa forte. Trabalho = obrigação.

grammar.sentence: You _____ go if you don't want.
grammar.explanation: "Don't / Do not have to" = não precisa, opcional. "Shouldn't / Should not" = não deveria (conselho).

grammar.sentence: She _____ buy groceries — we're out of milk.
grammar.explanation: "Needs to" = precisa. Outras opções também funcionam mas "needs to" é mais natural pra necessidade prática.

grammar.sentence: I _____ see a doctor about this.
grammar.explanation: "I should see" — sugestão suave. "Have to" seria mais forte.

grammar.sentence: She _____ leave at 7 — strict company rule.
grammar.explanation: "She has to leave" — obrigação imposta.
"We need to buy" — necessidade. "Need to" é o mais comum pra coisas práticas.
Modal + base, sem "to": "should study".
She → "has to".

grammar.passage: You should rest. I have to work tomorrow. We need to buy more milk. She doesn't have to come if she's busy.
grammar.question: O que o narrador tem que fazer amanhã?
grammar.explanation: O texto diz "I have to work tomorrow".

roleplay.scenario: Charlotte conta sua semana — você dá conselho, fala obrigações e necessidades.
roleplay.opening_line: My week is crazy — what should I do?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user gives advice with 'You should + base'
user uses 'I have to + base'
user uses 'We need to + base' or 'I need to + base'

roleplay.closing_cue: Charlotte fecha com "Three modals mastered!" quando obj_3 baterem.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Charlotte**: "My week is crazy — what should I do?"
2. **Student**: ~"You should rest."
3. **Charlotte**: "But I have so much work."
4. **Student**: ~"I have to study too."
5. **Charlotte**: "Misery loves company. What now?"
6. **Student**: ~"We need to take breaks."
7. **Charlotte**: "Three modals mastered!"

Should I...? / Do I have to...? (perguntas)
Diferenciar grau: should (sugestão) < need to < have to (obrigação)
